content.comment_body: Hello, Although I use analogue filter components to smooth analog inputs in my [product_name] programming software (which work well in simulation), they seem ineffective when used on my [product_name] hardware with article number [article_no]. This was disappointing to discover, but I've been working with it for nearly two years. Would the analogue filter function perform better on the newer [product_name] hardware with article number [article_no]? Thank you.

Your device is a 24 CE, not a 24 RCE. The 24 RCE version does not have analog inputs. It's challenging to assess such issues remotely. I don't believe upgrading to the latest [product_name] version will resolve this. It's difficult to evaluate your signal quality and instability from afar. You also haven't specified whether your signal is 0-10V or 0/4-20mA. Installation factors such as wiring type, cable quality, cable length and cross-section, and potential external interference (for example, from converters) can strongly influence performance.

The "Analog Filter" function samples every program cycle. The simulation environment runs much slower—possibly 10 or 20 times slower—than actual hardware. As a result, the filter time is much shorter on real hardware compared to simulation. When necessary, I first use the analog filter set to the maximum filter length, then add an "Average Value" block if I want the inputs to be averaged over longer periods.

Thank you for your helpful reply! Since your suggestion, I've added an average value block (8 samples over 1 second) after each analog filter on all sensor inputs, which has significantly reduced fluctuations. The filters are still set to 8 samples, but I plan to try different settings when I have more time. Much appreciated.
